what_it_does: This paper describes a receiver chip for small satellites operating at Ka-band (millimeter-wave frequency around 30 GHz) with 256 antenna elements forming a phased array (a grid of antennas that work together to steer signals electronically). Different satellite missions have different power and antenna requirements: smaller 10-kilogram satellites receive single-polarization signals (one orientation of radio waves) with low power consumption, while larger 100-kilogram satellites need to simultaneously receive dual-polarization signals (two orientations) from different directions with higher power. The paper's innovation is a switch-type quadrature-hybrid-first architecture that reconfigures between these modes flexibly without the power overhead of conventional receivers designed for just one mode.
